items.claim: The span and the confidence are right, and the row's central close fact is the strongest one in the chapter: at MT 18:9 the utterance signature stands last in the verse, with nothing following it, and MT 18:9 is the only verse in MT 18-19 where it does. Two smaller facts are wrong. First, the rationale's parenthetical offers MT 18:23 and MT 18:30 as the signature's non-final occurrences elsewhere in MT 18, but the witness carries five in that chapter - MT 18:3, 18:9, 18:23, 18:30 and 18:32 - of which four are non-final: 18:3, 18:23, 18:30 and 18:32. Naming two of the four understates the exclusivity the row is arguing. Second, the closed-section mark the witness places after MT 18:4 is argued in the rationale as onset corroboration from the far side of the seam, yet it is absent from this row's evidence refs, while each of its five sibling rows mirrors the far-side mark it argues (MT 18:20, 18:23, 18:26 and 18:32 respectively).
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 18:5 carries no onset device of its own, so its warrant is twofold and both parts are external to the verse - the thesis of the disputation is completed at MT 18:4 and the witness closes a section after it, and MT 18:5 then begins the first case-law protasis. Close side: MT 18:9 ends on the utterance signature in final position, and the witness sets no mark on that verse; the row states that absence plainly rather than implying corroboration it does not have. MT 18:10 then opens the next case with the same device-free protasis pattern. The seam at MT 18:9/18:10 is therefore the one seam inside MT 18 carried by a formula alone with no paragraph corroboration, and it holds from both sides: a genuinely verse-final refrain closes before it, and a fresh protasis opens after it.

items.claim: MT 18:10-20 holds one legal argument across three generations and the witness offers no seam inside it. The single strict word-event onset in these two chapters stands at MT 18:1, outside this span; MT 18:10-18:19 carries no utterance signature, no recognition refrain and no messenger opening; and the witness sets no paragraph mark anywhere between MT 18:4 and MT 18:20. The close at MT 18:20 restates the thesis first stated at MT 18:4 and is corroborated three ways on that one verse - a closed-section mark after it, the only paseq occurrence recorded in MT 18, and the first textual-variant note of the chapter. The eleven-verse length sits one verse above the ruled target band, the row discloses it as such, and the confidence medium matches a close argued partly from the absence of any internal seam rather than from a device of its own.

Close side: MT 18:20 restates the governing rule and the witness closes a section after it; MT 18:21 then opens the mirror repentance case. The internal candidate at MT 18:13/18:14 was weighed and fails from both sides: MT 18:13 ends on a content-final rule but carries no mark, and MT 18:18 reaches back to the father's own offenses before the rule is drawn at MT 18:19-20, so the three cases are argued as one chain. items.claim: The span is right and survives from both sides, but the row's warrant and one of its signals do not. First, no oath formula falls in MT 18:21-18:23. The only occurrence of the oath in MT 18-19 is MT 18:3, in the preceding oracle, so both the signal key oath.as_i_live and the rationale's description of the signature at MT 18:23 as oath-adjacent assert a device this span does not carry. Second, the row makes the paragraph mark its sole stated close evidence - it says in terms that it is the mark, not formula-finality, that is used - and the mark layer is single-witness corroboration that informs a boundary and never settles one. Content-grade close evidence is present in the very verse the row quotes and goes unnamed: the rhetorical question at MT 18:23 completes the repentance case, which is why the case can close there at all.

Close side: the signature inside MT 18:23 is not verse-final and the row is right that a further clause follows it - the second half of the question. What closes the unit is that question reaching its end within MT 18:23, with the witness closing a section after that verse as corroboration; MT 18:24 then opens the mirror apostasy case with a fresh protasis. Weighed from both sides the seam at MT 18:23/18:24 stands; only the stated warrant needs the content fact named beside the mark, so that a tier-3 witness is not carrying the decision alone on a high-confidence row.

MT 18:24 and MT 18:26 open with near-identical wording - MT 18:24 with the conjunction prefixed to the infinitive, MT 18:26 without it and with different accentuation - and the onset run this row quotes collates to MT 18:24, the verse it cites, not to its near-twin. items.claim: The span, the confidence and the internal reasoning are right, and three stated facts are wrong, none of them moving a boundary. First, the signals carry a messenger opening, but no messenger opening falls anywhere in MT 18-19: the messenger census runs from MT 17:22 straight to MT 20:3, and a skeleton sweep of these two chapters returns zero. What the rationale actually quotes at MT 18:30 is the utterance signature, which is a different device with the opposite structural role. Second, the signals carry a formula-final close, which this row's own close reasoning denies: it states that the signature at MT 18:32 stands mid-verse and that the closing imperative clause and the paragraph mark carry the close. The bytes agree with the reasoning, so the signal contradicts both. The cluster's other rows use a content-final close signal for exactly this situation. Third, the editorial note at MT 18:29 is described as flagging the form against BHS; the note's own text records that the form is kept the same as BHS where the validity of the form might be questioned - agreement, not divergence.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the apostasy case closes at MT 18:26 with a closed-section mark after it, and MT 18:27 opens the positive repentance case with a device-free protasis. Close side: MT 18:32 ends the chapter on the summons to turn and live, with an open-section mark after it, and MT 19:1 opens on the lament command - a genre onset, not a continuation. The internal candidate at MT 18:29/18:30 was weighed and correctly rejected from both sides: the therefore at MT 18:30 answers the objection quoted at MT 18:29, the witness sets no mark between them, and the ruled condition for an internal cut here - a refrain-grade close standing before a fresh therefore - is not met, because MT 18:29 is an objection and not a refrain. The row also declines the translation paragraph break that falls before MT 18:30, which is the correct handling of a translation-layer signal.

items.claim: The decision this row had to get right, it gets right: MT 19 is a fourteen-verse chapter kept whole as a single lament, at medium_low with the frontier flag and the density disclosure the whole-chapter rule requires, and it is held whole against its own internal paragraph mark on the strength of the genre label the text itself supplies - the lament noun stands at MT 19:1 and twice again in the colophon at MT 19:14, and those are the only two verses in MT 18-19 that carry it. One stated fact is wrong: the signals carry a parable-class key, but MT 19 supplies no parable label. The two forms of the ruling root in this chapter - the participle in the scepters clause at MT 19:11 and the infinitive in the colophon at MT 19:14 - belong to the verb to rule, not to the genre noun, and the genre noun stands at MT 18:2 and MT 18:3, in the preceding oracle and not here. The figure shift the key is reaching for is real and is already carried by the row's prose and by its evidence ref at MT 19:10, so nothing is lost by dropping a genre claim the chapter does not support.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the preceding unit closes at MT 18:32 with an open-section mark after it, and MT 19:1 opens on the command to take up a lament - neither a word-event onset nor a son-of-man address, and the inventory places no son-of-man address anywhere in MT 18-19, so the row's negative statement about its own onset is exactly right. Close side: MT 19:14 names the composition a lament in its final clause and the witness sets an open-section mark after it; the next unit opens on a dated frame at MT 20:1, and this close also ends the surrounding undated collection. The internal candidate at MT 19:9/19:10 was weighed from both sides and correctly not taken: for a cut stand the open-section mark after MT 19:9 and the fresh vine figure opening at MT 19:10; against it stands the genre frame at MT 19:1 and MT 19:14, which is a text-supplied label and therefore the stronger signal, and the ruled treatment that keeps a lament-labelled unit whole. The row discloses the internal mark rather than passing over it, which is the right handling.

suggested_fix.fact: MT 19 carries no parable label; the genre label the text supplies for this chapter is the lament noun at MT 19:1 and MT 19:14, and the two ruling-root forms in the chapter belong to the verb to rule, so the figure shift should be recorded without a parable-class claim
suggested_fix.verse: MT 19:1 and MT 19:14 for the genre label; MT 19:11 and MT 19:14 for the ruling-root forms
